root_cause: The radios component is initialized on two separate modules for the same radio group (name='reminder'). Keyboard navigation between radios in different modules does not trigger change events in the module containing conditional content, so the conditional panel remains visible when the opt-out radio is selected.
repair_strategy: Combine the two radio modules into a single module in the HTML so that all radios in the group are within the same component instance. Additionally, add a change event listener to the radios component to handle keyboard-driven state changes, ensuring conditional visibility updates when arrow keys change the selected radio.

expected_accessibility_effect: Keyboard users can navigate between all reminder options (Email, Text message, I do not want reminders) using arrow keys, and the associated conditional panels (email address, mobile number) show/hide correctly, satisfying WCAG 2.1.1 (Keyboard) and 2.4.3 (Focus Order).
functional_risks: Combining modules changes the DOM structure but preserves visual layout due to existing CSS classes.
The change event listener may fire twice for mouse interactions (click and change), but setAttributes is idempotent.
No impact on form submission or validation behavior.
verification_requirements: Verify that selecting a radio via arrow keys updates aria-expanded and toggles the correct conditional panel visibility.
Verify that mouse clicks continue to work as before.
Verify that choosing 'Text message' then arrowing to 'I do not want reminders' hides the mobile number field.
Verify that choosing 'Email' shows the email input field.
Ensure no regression in existing form submission or validation behavior.
